overview.headline: Bernoulli equation linking static dynamic and total pressure in steady flow

keyPoints.point: Total pressure remains constant while static and dynamic pressure combine in flow
keyPoints.quote: We call this constant the total pressure pt of the flow.

keyPoints.point: Dynamic pressure depends on density times square of velocity divided by two
keyPoints.quote: The form of the dynamic pressure is the density times the square of the velocity divided by two.

keyPoints.point: Restricted form requires inviscid incompressible steady flow without heat addition
keyPoints.quote: the restrictions for this form are that the flow is inviscid, incompressible, steady, without heat addition

keyPoints.point: Static pressure integrated over airfoil surface gives total aerodynamic force
keyPoints.quote: The static pressure integrated along the entire surface of the airfoil gives the total aerodynamic force on the foil.

keyTerms.gloss: pressure from random molecular motion that remains when flow is ordered
keyTerms.quote: The remaining random motion of the molecules still produces a pressure called the static pressure.

keyTerms.gloss: pressure linked to ordered motion and momentum of flowing gas
keyTerms.quote: We call this pressure the dynamic pressure.

keyTerms.gloss: constant sum of static and dynamic pressure throughout flow
keyTerms.quote: We call this constant the total pressure pt of the flow.

keyTerms.gloss: flow without viscous dissipation of energy
keyTerms.quote: Assuming a steady, inviscid flow we have a simplified conservation of energy equation in terms of the enthalpy of the fluid:

keyTerms.gloss: path followed by flow where total pressure stays constant
keyTerms.quote: the total pressure is a constant along any streamline, but may vary from streamline to streamline
